atletico-futbol-club.summary: Atletico Futbol Club organizes its teams into tiers, specifically mentioning MLS NEXT and Elite Academy. There are no specific squad markers or age bands detailed on the website.

bvb-international-academy-washington.summary: BVB IA Washington runs Elite Academy (EA) teams at U11-U15 above its NPL and WPL teams, and the club says plainly that a player not selected for an EA team may be offered an NPL or WPL place instead. Its NPL/WPL sides are split by location — Eastside/Bellevue and Seattle — and are separate teams from each other. The Black & Yellow Academy serves ages 6-10. Age groups are single years on the August-to-July seasonal year.

cascade-fc.summary: Cascade FC runs Premier Soccer with a Jr. Academy below it, whose curriculum is built on the same playing principles and game model used through the rest of the club.

crossfire-premier.summary: Crossfire Premier runs year-round Premier teams from U9 up, with the top boys sides in the USSDA and the top girls sides in ECNL; below those, teams play RCL. Crossfire Jr Teams (the Crossfire Junior Program, U7-U10) is a separate recreational programme, not a tier of the Premier teams. The club's program chart is written by single birth year, U6 through U19.

dragons-fc.summary: Dragons FC plays competitively in the WPL Super and Classic leagues and runs recreational programs beside them. Its published recreational age groups are multi-year bands — 2006-2009, 2010-2011 and 2012-2017 — rather than single years.

eagleclaw-fc.summary: Eagleclaw FC prefixes a team with the programme it belongs to: EFC for its own sides and VCF for Valencia CF Academy Seattle, so EFC BU14 and VCF BU14 are two different teams. The Advanced Academy covers ages 13-18 and the Primary Academy 5-12, and the club forms no more than two teams per birth year and gender. Its teams play the Washington Premier League's Development League, out of Starfire in Tukwila.

eastside-fc.summary: Eastside FC names teams by level and by training hub at once. At U13-U19 the top two are ECNL and ECNL RL, always based in Preston; at U8-U12 Red and White are the top two, then Blue, Grey and Navy. West teams train in Bellevue and on Mercer Island, and a West side may sit at the same competitive level as a Blue or Grey in a given year. Ages are single birth-year bands with a stated August-to-July birth-date range.

emerald-city-fc.summary: Emerald City FC publishes its teams as a grid of age group against level, and the level is the column: EA, then Green, then White, then Blue, then Black for boys; Green, White and Blue for girls. So a BU12 Green and a BU12 White are two different teams. The Development Program covers U8-U10 with no cuts, and the selective teams from U11 to U19 are formed by tryout. Seattle's premier soccer club since 1979.

harbor-soccer-club.summary: Harbor Soccer Club runs an Elite Academy (EA) programme and Girls Academy Aspire (G.A) above its Premier Program, with Harbor Rising Academy at the youngest ages.

highline-premier-fc.summary: Highline Premier FC forms multiple teams within each age group and competes in the Washington Premier League (WPL) and the Regional Club League (RCL). It is adding the Elite Academy League (EA) as a national platform within its 11v11 boys pathway, so an Elite Academy side sits above the club's WPL and RCL teams rather than beside them. The club serves West Seattle.

kitsap-alliance-fc.summary: Kitsap Alliance names a team by age group and colour, and the colour is the level: Blue is the club's first team in an age group and White the second, with Pre-ECNL above them at U12. Teams in the top league division carry an N1 prefix, as in N1 BU13 Blue, so the same side may appear with or without it. Ages are single years on the August-to-July seasonal year, and the club also runs a Junior Soccer Academy.

lake-washington-premier-fc.summary: Lake Washington Premier FC plays in the WPL and the National Premier Leagues.

mt-rainier-fc.summary: Mt. Rainier FC runs its competitive side as separate programmes rather than as one ladder: tryouts place a player into Academy or Premier, with a Junior Academy at U8-U10 below them, and Futures and Recreational beside them. So an Academy team and a Premier team of the same age are two different teams. Age groups are single years on the new August-to-July seasonal year. The club is based in Buckley.

mukilteo-youth-soccer-club.summary: Mukilteo Youth Soccer Club separates Recreational, Select and Premier, and its competitive teams play under WPL and NSRL rules. Select and Premier are listed as distinct programmes, so two MYSC sides of the same age in different ones are different teams.

norpoint-soccer-club.summary: Norpoint runs recreational and select programs, with a separate Micro programme at the youngest ages. Its recreational age bands are written as ranges — U7-U9 and U10-U12.

north-kitsap-soccer-club.summary: North Kitsap gives each select side its own name rather than a colour or a number: Lady Berserkers, Norse Novas, Sound Vipers, Serpents, Shield Maidens, Valkyries, Tsunami, Avalanche, Thunder, Fury and Vortex all appear beside a birth year, so two NKSC teams of the same year are told apart by that name. Select runs U11-U18 with a Pre-Comp programme at U9-U10; some sides are single years and some two, as in Girls 2010/2011.

northshore-select-club.summary: Northshore Select Club (NSC) is the Select programme of the Northshore Youth Soccer Association, in its own words a middle ground between Premier and Recreational, for boys and girls U9-U19, playing the North Puget Sound League (NPSL). The association's Premier arm is Sound Football Club, listed beside it on the same programmes page — so an NSC side and a Sound FC side are two different teams run by one association.

northwest-united-fc.summary: Northwest United FC in the Skagit Valley puts its ECNL-RL teams at the top — the club calls them the highest level of play within the club — with RCL and NPSL sides below, listed separately for boys and girls, and an Academy at the youngest ages. Age groups are single years on the August-to-July seasonal year.

pacnw-sc.summary: PacNW runs ECNL and ECNL-RL at the top, then Pre-ECNL, then colour-named sides. The colour is the level, and which league it plays in is written beside it: Maroon, Blue and White teams play RCL, while Gold, Silver and Copper play NPSL — so Gold (RCL) and Gold (NPSL) are different teams. Age groups are single years with an August-to-July birth-date range. Southlake FC in Greater Renton/Tukwila and the Federal Way recreational programme are separate programmes run by the club.

pilchuck-soccer-alliance.summary: Pilchuck Soccer Alliance calls its competitive side Force: Force Select Soccer for ages 9-19 and Force Academy for ages 7-8, with recreational soccer for 7-19 beside them. A team published as Pilchuck Force is this club's select programme.

rayados-soccer-academy-northwest.summary: Rayados Soccer Academy-Northwest, the official academy of CF Monterrey Rayados, runs three named stages rather than one ladder: Mini-Stripes at U5-U6, Junior Academy at U7-U9 and Academy at U10-U15, each described as preparing players for the next. So a Junior Academy side and an Academy side are different programmes.

seattle-celtic.summary: Seattle Celtic states its ladder outright: its top boys teams from the 2013 to 2008 age groups play the MLS Next League and its top girls teams the Girls Academy League, its second top boys teams play the Elite Academy League, and all other Celtic league teams play the WPL. So an MLS Next side, an Elite Academy side and a WPL side of the same age are three different teams. Age-bands run August 1 to July 31 and are written as two-year bands — a player born September 2013 is in the 2013/14 band and one born March 2013 is in the 2012/13 band. Below the league teams sit Development Teams at U8-U10, Pre-Dev at U7-U10 and the Celtic Óg Micro Academy at 4-6.

seattle-reign-academy.summary: Seattle Reign Academy runs Girls Academy (GA) at U13-U19, Aspire at U11-U12 and a Pre-Academy at U8-U12, so the programme a team belongs to is set by its age as much as by its level. Several Seattle Reign FC first-team players work as assistant coaches in the Academy.

seattle-united.summary: Seattle United names a team by birth year, then by level, then by region. The top sides are ECNL and ECNL RL, then Pre-ECNL, then Copa, Tango, Samba and Nova. Below those sit the regional teams — Shoreline, Northwest and South — each fielding Blue, then White, then Black. So Northwest and South are different teams, not one team written twice, and Copa is not Tango. A name like B13 means born 2013, not under-13.

sound-football-club.summary: Sound FC runs MLS NEXT for boys and Girls Academy Aspire for girls above its Premier teams, which play the Regional Club League; below those sit the Juniors programme at U8-U10 and a Goalkeeping Academy. Tryouts are advertised by league pair for each age — MLS Next/RCL, GA Aspire/RCL — so a club side may be named for either. Ages are single years, U8 for 2018 births through U19 for 2007. The club is in Woodinville.

south-kitsap-soccer-club.summary: South Kitsap Soccer Club fields its premier teams under a separate name, SK United, with recreational soccer beside it in three bands — Micro at U5-U8, Mod at U9-U10 and regulation play at U11-U19. A team published as SK United is this club's premier side.

sozo-fc.summary: Sozo FC names a premier team by birth year and colour — Boys 2013 Gold and Boys 2013 Royal are two different sides of the same birth year, and Gold appears in almost every year while Royal appears only in some. Some teams carry a two-year band instead, as in Boys 2007/08 Gold. The club plays the Regional Club League (RCL) and runs Sozo Academy below its premier teams.

sparta-tacoma.summary: Sparta Tacoma is the premier-level, year-round programme of North Tacoma Soccer Club, for players 7 to 19. Its boys teams play the Elite Academy (EA) League, which the club says is for its highest level (red) boys teams from 2015/U11 through 2007-2008/U18/19 — so red is the top level here, not one squad among equals. Teams below that play up to 16 Washington Premier League games a season. The club writes an age both ways, as a birth year and as a U-number.

united-sports-fc.summary: United Sports FC runs a Winter Cubs Academy for birth years 2014 to 2018.

valor-soccer.summary: Valor Soccer places players by tryout into three competitive programmes — Elite, Premier and Select — with Recreational beside them. Elite is the club's top level and covers its ECNL-RL, MLS Next and GA Aspire teams; Premier plays RCL, and Select plays NPSL with the flexibility to keep other activities a priority. So a Valor Premier side and a Valor Select side of the same age are two different teams. The club is in Maple Valley and was founded in 2019.

warriors.summary: The club publishes itself as Warriors Sports Academy, and Little Warriors Sports Academy is its junior programme — a different thing, not the same name shortened. Teams are named by age group and league: the EA sides (U11 EA through U18 EA) are the top level, and the WPL sides carry Attack, as in U14 Attack. At U9 and U10 there are two Attack teams in the age group, told apart by colour — U10 Attack Blue and U10 Attack Gold. Age groups run August 1 to July 31.

washington-east-surf-soccer-club.summary: Washington East Surf runs Elite Academy and Girls Academy programmes alongside Surf Select, with academy sessions held separately in Spokane and in the Columbia Basin — so a side named for one location is not the same team as one named for the other.

washington-premier-fc.summary: Washington Premier FC names a team by birth year and level, and the level is a colour once past ECNL: ECNL, then ECNL RL, then Pre-ECNL, then Black, White, Navy and Gold. A B15 Black and a B15 Navy are two different teams in the same age group, not one written twice. The tryout results write the two halves in either order, B10 Black or Black B10. Everything trains at the club's Puyallup complex; Washington United is its separate recreational programme in Pierce County.

washington-rush.summary: Washington Rush separates Premier (ages 7-18, its top level), Select (9-18, a bridge between recreational and premier without the year-round commitment) and Junior RCL (7-8). Above Premier it fields Girls Academy and MLS NEXT teams, which the club prices separately. Mighty Mites and the Junior Academy are its youngest programmes. It is the regional club for the North County Youth Soccer Association and part of the international Rush network.

wenatchee-fa.summary: Wenatchee FA is the club formed by WFC Youth and Wenatchee United together, and it publishes every team as a two-year band plus a colour: B12/13 ECNL-RL Black, B12/13 Red, B12/13 White, B12/13 Grey. The colour is the level — Black is the top side in an age group and carries the ECNL-RL label where the club fields one, then Red, then White, then Grey. Its competition pathway runs ECNL-RL, then RCL and RCL/N1, then WPL Classic/Copa, with PAL at U10-U12 and a development WPL at U9-U10.

west-sound-soccer-academy.summary: West Sound Soccer Academy is a women-led, girls-first club whose teams are grouped as Junior Academy (U9-U10), Academy (U11-U14) and High School Academy (U15-U19), and it plays WPL. How many teams form at an age depends on how many players register and how many coaches are available.

western-washington-surf.summary: Western Washington Surf fields boys' and girls' teams at Elite and Premier levels. Elite is split into Elite North and Elite South, each with an A Team and a B Team. Premier is run town by town — Tacoma, Medina, Redmond, Puyallup and others each publish their own season outline with A Teams and B&C Teams — so two Surf sides of the same age in different towns are different teams. Season outlines group ages in pairs (U9 & U10, U11 & U12) while teams are named by single birth year. Their pages name the leagues each level plays: EA League and DPL for the Elite A teams, NPL and WPL below, and JDL at U6-U7.

whatcom-fc-rangers.summary: Whatcom FC Rangers put their ECNL RL side at the top of each age group from U13 up, with colour-named teams below it — Gold and Blue — and the club writes a team either by birth year (2009 Gold) or by age group (U16/U17 Blue). Age groups run on the August-to-July seasonal year. Jr Rangers is the programme for players not ready for premier soccer.
